caption: The drawing depicts two elongated decorative objects, both appearing to be ornate hairpins or jewelry pieces, set against a plain, light beige background. Each object is primarily composed of gold-colored elements and round, white or pale gray beads arranged in vertical sequences. The object on the left has a gold leaf-shaped base adorned with a cluster of five round beads near the top, three arranged horizontally and two placed just below, with the largest bead at the center. Below the cluster, a string of smaller gold beads and three additional larger round beads are vertically aligned, each separated by small gold segments, and ending in a long, thin gold pin extending downward. The object on the right shows a gold curved hook at the top, possibly an earring; beneath the hook, four white or gray round beads are connected by short gold chains with tiny gold beads forming clusters between them, and a longer gold pin extends down from the last bead. The arrangement on this object suggests a cascading effect of beads and gold elements. The drawing is signed "JOHN. H. TERCUZZI" in the lower left corner and is dated "MAR. 1938." in small text at the upper right corner.
title: Cap or Bonnet Pin
